chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn Umar, from Abdullah ibn Ayoob, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
I guarantee that whoever is frugal will never become poor.
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam guarantee for those who practice frugality?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) assurance that 'moderation' (iqtisad) serves as a divine guarantee against poverty, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balanced consumption rather than extreme asceticism or extravagance. This principle aligns with the Quranic description of the righteous who are neither wasteful nor stingy, positioning financial prudence as a spiritual discipline that secures material sufficiency through divine providence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-32 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Ali ibn Isma’il, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Umar, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ayoob, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Maymun said, “I heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say, ‘
I guarantee that whoever is frugal will never become poor.’”
